references.text: The Israelites also complained here that they had left Egypt and longed for the food they had there, even though they were slaves.
The people again complained about the food in the wilderness and expressed dissatisfaction with the manna, just as in this verse.
Describes the hard slave labor in Egypt, which stands in contrast to the people's idealized memories of the food they received there.
The Israelites grumbled against Moses and Aaron and wished to return to Egypt, a recurring theme of longing to go back.
Describes the manna that God gave them in the wilderness, which the people now complain about compared to the food in Egypt.
Stephen refers to the Israelites' desire to return to Egypt in his speech, reflecting this event.
